# rpi — a Rust-native coding-agent runtime **English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rpi-cli.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/crates/d/rpi-cli.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) [![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli) [![license](https://img.shields.io/crates/l/rpi-cli.svg)](#license) [![MSRV](https://img.shields.io/badge/MSRV-1.88-blue.svg)](#install) [![CI](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/bigfish1913/pi-rust?style=flat)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/stargazers) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/bigfish1913/pi-rust)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/releases/latest) [![Best of Agent Harnesses](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%8F%86_Best_of-Agent_Harnesses-5ac4bf)](https://github.com/RyanAlberts/best-of-Agent-Harnesses) `rpi` is a library-first coding-agent runtime written in Rust, plus a terminal agent built on top of it. Eleven composable crates span provider adapters, a durable crash-resumable agent loop, a reusable runtime, a terminal UI, and a stable plugin ABI — so the same code works as an embedded SDK or as a ready-to-run `rpi` command. rpi began as a Rust reimplementation of the [Pi TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) by Mario Zechner. It now includes its own Rust-native plugin ABI and execution infrastructure. See [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements) and [NOTICE](NOTICE) for upstream attribution. [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Website](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/) · [Docs](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/docs.html) · [Extension catalog and submissions](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/packages.html?lang=en) · [rpi-extension](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension) ## See it in action ![rpi TUI reading a project README and displaying the run and test commands](docs/images/rpi-interactive.png) **Terminal.** Run `rpi` in a project directory. The screenshot shows an isolated sample session and a `read` tool call. [User guide](docs/guides/user-guide.md) ![rpi-web with a project sidebar, tool activity and a Markdown reply](docs/images/rpi-web.png) **Web.** Install with `rpi install rpi-web`, then run `rpi --webserver` in your project directory and open the address it prints. [Web setup guide](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension/tree/main/packages/rpi-web) ![RPI Work desktop preview with a conversation and a Git diff side by side](docs/images/rpi-work-desktop.png) **Desktop.** RPI Work’s GPUI preview shows project sessions, conversation and Git diffs in a native window. [RPI Work](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-work)
Terminal and SDK recordings ![rpi terminal demo — opening the built-in help without a model request](docs/images/rpi-tui-demo.gif) Open the terminal agent and explore `/help`, with no real API key or model request. Recording script: [`demo/tui.tape`](demo/tui.tape). ![rpi SDK demo — an agent loop and a real tool round-trip, offline with the faux provider](docs/images/rpi-sdk-demo.gif) The agent loop and a real `write` tool round-trip, recorded with no API key and no network — the same path the tests take. Source of truth is [`demo/sdk.tape`](demo/sdk.tape); regenerate with `task demo`.
## Three ways to use it | You want | Depend on | Start at | | -------- | --------- | -------- | | A working terminal coding agent | nothing | `cargo install rpi-cli` | | Your own agent inside your process | `rpi-agent` (+ `rpi-ai`, `rpi-tools`) | [`examples/minimal`](examples/minimal) | | A tool/provider that extends every session | `rpi-plugin-sdk` | [`examples/plugin-stub`](examples/plugin-stub) | The three share one implementation. Build your tools once, debug them inside an embedded agent, and ship the same code as a `cdylib` plugin that the global `rpi` loads. See [`docs/agent/project-structure.md`](docs/agent/project-structure.md) for the recommended project layout. ## Install **Prebuilt binary** (no Rust toolchain needed): ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/main/scripts/install.sh | sh ``` Verifies the published SHA-256 checksum and installs to `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`. Preview first with `--dry-run`. On **Windows (x64)**, run in PowerShell 5.1 or later: ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/main/scripts/install.ps1).Content)) ``` Verifies the published SHA-256 checksum and installs to `$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\rpi`. Follow the printed instructions to add it to PATH, then run `rpi --version`. Append `-DryRun` to preview, or use `-Version ` and `-Dir 'C:\Tools\rpi'` to select a version and directory. **From npm** (requires Node.js 20+; no Rust toolchain needed): ```bash npm install -g @bigfishnpm/rpi rpi --version ``` The npm installer downloads the matching GitHub Release binary and verifies both archive and executable SHA-256 checksums pinned in the package. It supports macOS (x64/ARM64), Windows (x64), and Linux (x64 glibc/musl and ARM64 glibc). **From crates.io** (requires Rust 1.88+): ```bash cargo install rpi-cli rpi --version ``` **Package managers:** ```bash brew tap bigfish1913/tap && brew install rpi # macOS (Apple silicon), Linux scoop bucket add bigfish1913 https://github.com/bigfish1913/scoop-bucket scoop install rpi # Windows ``` The Homebrew formula currently supports Apple silicon on macOS. Intel Macs can use the prebuilt installer for releases with an `x86_64-apple-darwin` asset, or `cargo install rpi-cli`. A winget manifest is [open for review](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/pull/444745). **From source:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust.git cd pi-rust && cargo run -p minimal # offline agent, no API key required ``` Real output of the two offline examples — no credentials, no network, identical bytes every run. Regenerate with `task demo-transcript`: ```text $ cargo run -q -p minimal minimal example: 2 messages after run - user - assistant assistant reply: Hello from the faux provider! AgentEnd observed. $ cargo run -q -p tools-example tools example: 4 messages after run wrote out.txt (28 bytes): "hello from the tools example" AgentEnd observed; tool ran against OsExecutionEnv. ``` ## Quick start ### The CLI ```bash export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... # or OPENAI_API_KEY for OpenAI rpi # interactive TUI rpi -p "summarize the README" # one-shot rpi --mode json -p "list the crates" # machine-readable event stream rpi --mini -p "explain this error" # one-shot without saving the session ``` `--mini` uses in-memory sessions and disables native durable execution. The conversation ends with the process, and session import, export, fork, and resume are unavailable. Context compaction, tools, and resource discovery work as usual. Use `--tools read` to limit the tool set to `read`, or `-p` for a one-shot reply. Sessions persist as JSONL and survive a crash mid-run; `rpi` resumes from the last committed frame rather than replaying the turn. ### Model configuration For a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway, save the [example JSON](examples/models.example.json) as `models.json` in your agent directory. Create the directory if needed. If `models.json` already exists, add the `gateway` entry under its `providers` object. | Environment | `models.json` path | | --- | --- | | macOS / Linux | `~/.rpi/agent/models.json` | | Windows | `%USERPROFILE%\.rpi\agent\models.json` | | Custom agent directory | `models.json` inside the absolute directory set by `RPI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` | ```json { "providers": { "gateway": { "api": "openai-completions", "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1", "apiKey": "$RPI_GATEWAY_API_KEY", "models": [ { "id": "your-model-id", "name": "My Gateway Model" } ] } } } ``` Replace `baseUrl` and `your-model-id` with the values from your provider. Set the key in the shell where you launch rpi. - macOS / Linux — `export RPI_GATEWAY_API_KEY='your-api-key'` - Windows PowerShell — `$env:RPI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = 'your-api-key'` ```bash rpi auth check --provider gateway rpi --model gateway/your-model-id ``` Use the same model ID in the launch command and in the JSON file. The user guide also covers [Anthropic-compatible gateways](docs/guides/user-guide.md#自定义-provider). ### Runtime diagnostics To investigate slow model preparation, context construction, tool execution, or persistent assistant-frame writes, temporarily enable stderr diagnostics: ```bash RPI_AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS=1 RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS=1 \ rpi -p "reproduce the issue" 2>rpi-diagnostics.log ``` `RPI_AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS` reports context, request, tool, and session append latencies. `RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS` reports durable frame batching, flush barriers, and writer failures. Diagnostics are disabled when the variables are unset or set to `0`; they do not change the JSONL format. See [`docs/debugging/rust-debugging.md`](docs/debugging/rust-debugging.md) for the field reference. The built-in read-only `docs` tool can retrieve it with `{"topic":"debugging","query":"RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS"}`. ### Request timeouts and model compatibility `--timeout 600` limits a whole LLM request, including its streamed response. `--stream-idle-timeout 300` independently limits silence between response body bytes after the response starts. Every non-empty chunk resets the idle timer, including SSE keepalives and partial frames. A stalled stream produces a retryable error; the configured retry policy controls whether it is retried. Healthy streams may run longer than the idle timeout, up to the total deadline. Use `--stream-idle-timeout 0` to disable the idle timer. You can also set `"streamIdleTimeout": 300` (seconds) in `~/.rpi/agent/settings.json`; the CLI flag takes precedence. `httpIdleTimeout` only expires unused pooled connections and does not control an active response. For providers with `"api": "openai-completions"`, put compatibility flags in each model's `compat` object in `~/.rpi/agent/models.json`, for example: ```json "compat": { "thinkingFormat": "deepseek", "requiresReasoningContent": true } ``` `requiresReasoningContent` replays assistant thinking in `reasoning_content`, including an empty string for assistant messages without thinking. The pi name `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages` is accepted as an alias; if both are present, the rpi spelling wins and conflicting values produce a warning. `thinkingFormat` supports `"openai"` (the default request shape) and `"deepseek"` (also sends `thinking: { "type": "enabled" | "disabled" }` for reasoning-capable models). `supportsReasoningEffort: false` suppresses `reasoning_effort` if the gateway does not accept it. `requiresThinkingAsText` instead places thinking in ordinary text content. Unknown compat fields and invalid values produce warnings naming the provider and model; invalid compat objects are ignored. Other pi thinking formats are not currently supported. ### The SDK Build an agent against a deterministic in-process provider — no API key, no network, no flakiness: ```rust use rpi_agent::AgentBuilder; use rpi_ai::providers::faux::{FauxProvider, FauxScript}; use rpi_ai::Provider; #[tokio::main] async fn main() { // `FauxProvider::new` already returns an `Arc`. let provider = FauxProvider::new(FauxScript::new().with_text("Hello from the faux provider!")); let model = provider.default_model().clone(); let agent = AgentBuilder::new() .model(model) .system_prompt("You are a helpful assistant.") .stream_fn(make_stream_fn(provider)) .build() .expect("agent builds"); let mut events = agent.subscribe(); agent.prompt("hi").await.expect("prompt completes"); while let Ok(ev) = events.try_recv() { let _ = ev; // AgentEvent::{MessageUpdate, ToolEnd, AgentEnd, …} } println!("{} messages after the run", agent.state().messages.len()); } ``` `make_stream_fn` bridges the synchronous `StreamFn` contract to the async provider — the full version is in [`examples/minimal/src/main.rs`](examples/minimal/src/main.rs) (`cargo run -p minimal`). ## Crates Eleven workspace crates, one shared version. Dependency direction is one-way and enforced in review: ``` rpi-telemetry → rpi-ai → rpi-agent → rpi-tools → rpi-harness ↘ rpi-runtime ``` Six crates sit outside that chain: - `rpi-durable` provides backend-independent checkpoint validation and progress projection for `rpi-harness`; it has no `rpi-*` dependencies. It is a native library, distinct from the workflow extension of the same name. - `rpi-tui` depends on no other `rpi-*` crate. - `rpi-runtime` depends on `rpi-ai` and provides embeddable model catalogs, credential resolution and execution bindings. See the [runtime guide](docs/architecture/reusable-runtime.md). - `rpi-plugin-sdk` is a leaf too (it has no `rpi-*` deps), but it is not only the host's plugin contract: `rpi-tools` also reads its env-var names, so the host and its plugins cannot disagree about the strings they exchange across the ABI. That edge is names-only — nothing is linked or called. - `rpi-extensions` is `rpi-plugin-sdk` plus `rpi-ai`/`rpi-agent`, since it hosts plugins that run tools. - `rpi-cli` brings together the TUI, the harness and the plugin loader, with `rpi-durable` included through `rpi-harness`. | Crate | What it is | | ----- | ---------- | | [`rpi-telemetry`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-telemetry) | Span/event contracts with a no-op default — instrumentation is opt-in, and pulls in no tracing or OpenTelemetry backend | | [`rpi-ai`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-ai) | Provider-agnostic message, streaming and tool-schema types; Anthropic + OpenAI-compatible + `faux` providers | | [`rpi-runtime`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-runtime) | Embeddable model catalog, credential resolution, model selection and execution bindings | | [`rpi-agent`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-agent) | The agent loop: `AgentTool`, events, hooks, queues, cancellation | | [`rpi-tools`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-tools) | `read`/`write`/`edit`/`bash` (+ `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `powershell`) and the `ExecutionEnv` seam | | [`rpi-durable`](crates/rpi-durable) | Backend-independent checkpoint validation and assistant-progress projection; no tool execution or storage backend | | [`rpi-harness`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-harness) | Session tree, JSONL persistence, compaction, crash recovery, the run loop | | [`rpi-tui`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-tui) | Terminal UI primitives: components, layout, editor, transcript rendering | | [`rpi-cli`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) | The `rpi` binary: TUI, one-shot and JSON modes, config, plugin loading | | [`rpi-plugin-sdk`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-plugin-sdk) | The stable `#[repr(C)]` ABI contract for plugins. No `rpi-*` deps; only `serde_json`, behind a default `json` feature that can be turned off | | [`rpi-extensions`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-extensions) | Host-side plugin loader and the async-across-ABI tool bridge | Every crate has its own README and docs.rs page. The `crates/rpi-*` directories and the published crate names use the same `rpi-` prefix. ## Why rpi Most coding agents are CLIs. `rpi` is a **runtime with a CLI attached**, which changes what you can build with it: - **Embeddable.** The agent loop is a library. `rpi-agent` + `rpi-ai` is enough to run an agent inside your own process, with your own event handling and output — no shelling out to a tool and scraping stdout. - **Testable offline.** A deterministic `faux` provider and an in-memory execution environment are first-class, not mocks bolted on. `rpi-ai` puts its real HTTP providers behind a `providers` feature flag, so your test suite cannot silently depend on the network for the paths you exercise. - **Durable.** Sessions are a tree with JSONL persistence and per-frame progress. Recovery resumes from committed progress; it does not guarantee exactly-once external side effects. Tools still need appropriate idempotency and recovery checks. - **Extensible across a stable boundary.** Plugins are Rust `cdylib`s behind a hand-written, panic-contained C ABI with version negotiation — the ABI survives compiler and crate version skew, so extensions do not break on every release. - **One implementation, two surfaces.** The global CLI and an embedded agent load the same tools. You do not maintain a plugin and a library variant separately. ### How it compares Structural differences against other terminal coding agents. Facts about other tools are as of 2026-09 and change often — check their documentation; only the `rpi` column is maintained here. | | rpi | Claude Code | Codex CLI | opencode | aider | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Language | Rust | TypeScript | Rust | TypeScript/Go | Python | | Source available | ✅ MIT | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Usable as an embedded library | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ⚠️ | ⚠️ | | First-class plugin ABI | ✅ | hooks/MCP | ❌ | plugin API | ❌ | | Headless server + remote client | ✅ | ⚠️ | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ | | Provider-agnostic gateways | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | If you want the most polished single-vendor experience, use the vendor's tool. `rpi` is for people who want to own the loop. rpi is listed in [Best of Agent Harnesses](https://github.com/RyanAlberts/best-of-Agent-Harnesses) under *Coding agent products*, scored **bounded** and **durable** — the durable score comes from the crash-resumable JSONL sessions. ## Performance Measured on Windows 11 (x86_64), rustc 1.97.1, `--release`. Both scripts rebuild and re-measure on your own machine. `sh scripts/bench.sh` — standalone numbers: | Metric | Value | | ------ | ----- | | Release binary size | **21.8 MiB** | | `rpi --version` wall time | **~17 ms** median | | RSS once the agent is ready | **12.0 MiB** | `node scripts/bench-vs-pi.mjs --pi ` — against native Pi on the same machine, both offline, each with a fresh isolated config directory: | Metric | rpi (Rust) | pi (TypeScript) | Difference | | ------ | ---------: | --------------: | ---------- | | `--version` | **17.5 ms** | 169.5 ms | **9.7× faster** | | Cold start | **17.7 ms** | 189.5 ms | **10.7× faster** | | RSS at ready | **12.0 MiB** | 91.5 MiB | **7.6× smaller** | | Install footprint | **21.8 MiB** (one binary) | ~385 MiB (+ ~91 MiB Node) | **~18–22× smaller** | **Cold start** is spawn → the agent answering its first command: process creation plus full initialisation, excluding teardown and any LLM work. rpi's `--version` (17.5 ms) and cold start (17.7 ms) are effectively equal, so startup is process creation, not initialisation; Pi is dominated by Node boot. Isolation caveat: rpi reads `RPI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` / `RPI_OFFLINE`, native Pi reads `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` / `PI_OFFLINE`. Set the matching pair for each, or rpi silently loads the machine's global plugins. Method, raw per-run numbers, and what is *not* measured (LLM latency, tool-loop throughput, long sessions, TUI frame cost) are in [`docs/performance/benchmark-vs-pi.md`](docs/performance/benchmark-vs-pi.md). ## Plugins Plugins are Rust `cdylib` libraries behind a stable `#[repr(C)]` ABI. A plugin can register tools, providers, slash commands, event handlers, markdown renderers and discovered resources. ```bash rpi install rpi-todo # prebuilt extension; no Rust toolchain needed rpi install my-ext --path ../my-ext # local, for development rpi extension update [name] # all eligible extensions, or one by name rpi dev # build + watch + live reload ``` Use `rpi extension update` to update all project-linked extensions and globally installed registry/prebuilt extensions, or `rpi extension update ` to select one by name. Updates preserve the original Cargo build backend or explicit GitHub source. Global development installs made with `--path` are excluded. The old `rpi package update [name]` remains compatible; prefer `extension update` for extension updates. Project linking commands remain `rpi package link`, `rpi package list`, and `rpi package unlink`. The host loads project `.rpi/extensions`, then global `~/.rpi/agent/extensions`, then any `--extensions-dir`. For a new Rust plugin, start with [`docs/extensions/authoring.md`](docs/extensions/authoring.md) and `examples/plugin-stub`. Use `rpi-plugin-sdk` for the `cdylib` ABI. If the plugin project also needs reusable session, workspace, native RPC or durable-runtime logic for a Web/ACP adapter, add [`rpi-extcore`](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-extcore) (`rpi-extcore = "0.1"`). It is a normal Rust library, not the `cdylib` entry point, and it does not replace `rpi-plugin-sdk`; a simple tool plugin should not add it unnecessarily. Ready-to-install extensions live in the companion [`pi-rust/rpi-extension`](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension) repository, with an [online catalog](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/packages.html?lang=en). The catalog moved from `pi-rust/rpi-package` to `pi-rust/rpi-extension`. Both spellings identify the same publisher: existing installs (including records that only stored a `prebuilt:` marker), `--github pi-rust/rpi-package` invocations, and the previous CDN prefix keep working, while version discovery and startup update checks follow the move and rewrite the recorded source. Browse the catalog for install commands, or open the [`packages/` source directory](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension/tree/main/packages) for extension READMEs and examples. Start with `rpi install rpi-todo` above, then use the [extension authoring guide](docs/extensions/authoring.md) to build your own. ### Web access Web access is optional, not part of the CLI's default tool set: ```bash rpi install rpi-websearch # websearch: titles, URLs and snippets rpi install rpi-webfetch # webfetch: readable text from public pages ``` Restart rpi after installation to load the tools. These extensions do not provide an interactive browser: clicking, login flows and page JavaScript execution require separate browser tooling. ### Subagents with inherited configuration Install the companion `rpi-subagents` extension to expose `delegate_task`: ```bash rpi install rpi-subagents ``` The host snapshots the parent's effective model/provider binding, thinking level, system prompt, resources, request options, active tools, project cwd and approval hooks. It does not reconstruct CLI defaults or pass credentials through plugin JSON. Each child runs in a separate in-memory session without copying or modifying the parent's conversation history. The host API can narrow the inherited tool set, never expand it; `delegate_task` is excluded and recursive delegation is rejected. Approvals use the parent's UI, and parent completion or cancellation stops the child. This is capability inheritance and session isolation, not an OS sandbox. Use a compatible host and subagent extension; unsupported hosts fail explicitly rather than falling back to a differently configured subprocess. Rust callers use `AgentHarness::create_child`. Extensions read the active bindings with `GetExecutionContext` and manage runs with `IndependentRun`. `ChildAgent` remains available for compatibility with released extensions. See the [subagent protocol](docs/extensions/subagents.md) for lifecycle and limits. ### Authoring an extension ```rust use rpi_plugin_sdk::{export_plugin, StbStringRef}; export_plugin!(|api| { if let Some(declare) = api.declare { declare(StbStringRef::from_str(r#"{"priority":60,"platforms":["linux"]}"#)); } // register tools / handlers through `api` 0 }); ``` Start from [`examples/plugin-stub`](examples/plugin-stub) — a complete plugin with the full `execute`→`poll`→`cancel`→`destroy` lifecycle — and read [`docs/extensions/authoring.md`](docs/extensions/authoring.md) for the safety rules, which are load-bearing rather than stylistic. ## Shared local Host on Unix `rpi --host [area]` runs independent Agent Sessions in one local Host process per area. It supports the ordinary interactive TUI, stdio RPC, and one-shot Mini with `rpi --host [area] --mini "prompt"`. The `default` area uses ordinary Session storage. Other areas use `local-host-v1/area-/sessions` under the agent home unless an explicit Session directory is supplied. A named area can set `maxAgents` (default 32, range 1–256) and `idleTimeoutSeconds` (default 0, disabled). ## Persistent Shared Host areas on macOS ```bash rpi --native-host # Open the default area's Session in the terminal rpi --native-host work # Open a separate area and Session rpi --native-host --mode json # Inspect the selected area, Host and Session IDs ``` First entry creates `$RPI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/host.json` (normally `~/.rpi/agent/host.json`) and starts a detached Host. With the default settings, it starts one Persistent Agent. Clients that select the same Agent share its Session. Start each client from the workspace configured for its Agent. The settings file starts with `{"defaultArea":"default","areas":{"default":{}}}`. Each area can set `provider`, `model`, `tools`, and `maxAgents`. The optional `recovery` object accepts `restore_on_start` and `restart_on_crash`, for example `{"restore_on_start":true,"restart_on_crash":false}`. Omitting `recovery` enables both for a named area. Within an explicit object, omitted switches default to `false`. The capacity and recovery settings are written when the private area configuration is first generated. The initial profile uses global model settings and available non-OAuth credentials. Its tool list defaults to `read`. The generated private profile and Host configuration live under `hosts//` and are reused on restart. `--mode json` prints the configuration path for [the Host control commands](crates/rpi-cli/src/host/cli.rs), including `status` and `administrative-stop`. Set an area's `runTimeoutMs` before first entry to give each Persistent operation an execution deadline in milliseconds. The deadline starts after admission. The daemon signals cancellation at the deadline, then waits for the operation and its Session writes to settle. The generated private Host configuration stores the value at `host.default_timeouts.run_ms` and accepts an optional `host.hard_timeout_limits.run_ms`. Set `shutdownGraceMs` before first entry to report a Persistent Agent that is still closing after that many milliseconds during signal or administrative shutdown. The daemon continues waiting for settlement before completing shutdown. The private Host configuration stores the value at `host.default_timeouts.shutdown_grace_ms` and accepts an optional `host.hard_timeout_limits.shutdown_grace_ms`. A daemon with Mini control enabled requires shared Agent timer defaults to be unset. Set `idleTimeoutMs` or `disconnectedTimeoutMs` in an area before first entry. The generated private configuration stores these values as `host.default_timeouts.idle_ms` and `host.default_timeouts.disconnected_ms`. On expiry, the idle timer can release a Persistent Agent's Session writer and capacity slot after settlement. An authenticated area Session connection keeps its Agent loaded. Set `host.default_timeouts.disconnected_ms` for an Agent with an area Session route to start a separate deadline when its last authenticated Session connection leaves. A new connection clears that deadline. If both timers are set, the first expired deadline applies once the Agent has settled and no Session peers remain. Running work and pending Session work retain the owner. Optional caps use the corresponding `host.hard_timeout_limits` fields. The timers and `restoreOnAttach` require `restore` permission. When any of these area settings is enabled, the generated administrative policy grants `restore` and `cancel` to all declared members. Use `host inspect` and `host profiles` to get the current `Unloaded` revision and frozen profile reference, then run `host administrative-restore` to reopen the original Agent and Session. Area terminal and stdio RPC clients can then reconnect to that Session in the same daemon. Set `restoreOnAttach: true` before first entry to let an authenticated Session connection restore an `Unloaded` member directly from its frozen profile. This option is off by default. It uses the same capacity and Session writer checks as explicit Restore and leaves the administrative receipt journal for explicit requests. An administratively `Closed` member still requires explicit Restore. Administrative Close accepts an `Unloaded` revision, ends any Session connections on a loaded owner, and removes the member from configured recovery. For a daemon that can run without loaded Agents, set `host.host_idle_timeout_ms` in its private configuration. It shuts down after that many consecutive milliseconds with zero resident Agents and zero control or Session connections. An in-progress lifecycle transaction can delay shutdown. To configure more Persistent Agents in one area, add `"agentProfiles":[{"name":"review","path":"/absolute/private/review.json"}]` to its settings before first entry. Each [private Agent profile](crates/rpi-cli/src/host/profile.rs) supplies its own Agent ID, Session ID and path, and workspace. The default Agent counts toward `maxAgents`. Initialize the area from the default Agent's workspace. Open a declared member from its own workspace with `rpi --native-host work --agent review`, adding `--mode json` or `--mode rpc` as needed. The private area configuration stores those profile references and starts the declared Agents with the default member. Set `"restoreAreas":["default","work"]` in the top-level `host.json` and declare each listed area under `areas`. Run `rpi --native-host --restore-areas` to bring the listed daemons up together from any workspace. Each area must already have a private daemon configuration with `restore_on_start` enabled. The command validates all listed configurations before starting any daemon, reuses running areas, and reports each result as JSON. The list is an explicit recovery policy. An area stopped with `administrative-stop` starts again on the next group restore if it is still listed. Set `"defaultTerminal":true` in the top-level `host.json` to open the default area's Agent when you run bare `rpi` from that Agent's workspace in a terminal. Initialize the area with `rpi --native-host` first. Calls with arguments, redirected input or output, and other workspaces continue through the ordinary CLI. The Host terminal provides shared chat, history, and cancellation. Use the ordinary CLI entry points for the local session picker and extension UI. The terminal supports shared text prompts, live responses, saved history, and cancellation. Use `/thinking ` while the Agent is idle to change the thinking level for subsequent prompts. All connected terminals for that Agent show the new level. Stdio RPC clients can use `set_thinking_level` and receive `thinking_level_changed`. The setting lasts while the Agent stays loaded. Restoring the Agent uses its frozen profile again. Closing a terminal disconnects its view. ## Remote mode ```bash rpi --server # headless agent over TCP, prints an auth token rpi --connect host:port --token T # TUI client with zero local agent resources ``` The client holds no provider, tools, extensions or session files — all agent work happens on the server, so a thin terminal anywhere can drive a beefy machine. See [`docs/remote/user-guide.md`](docs/remote/user-guide.md). ## Project status | | | | --- | --- | | Current release | **[0.31.0](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/releases)** (eleven workspace crates, one shared version) | | Stability | `rpi-ai`, `rpi-agent`, `rpi-tools`, `rpi-harness`, `rpi-plugin-sdk` are the intended stable surface | | MSRV | 1.88 | | Platforms | Linux (GNU and musl), macOS, Windows (CI runs the suite on Linux) | | Binary release targets | Linux (x86_64 GNU/musl, aarch64 GNU), macOS (Intel/Apple silicon), Windows (x86_64) | `rpi` is a self-contained Rust coding-agent stack. No Node component is required and none is loaded. ## Documentation Start with the [documentation index](docs/README.md), grouped by feature. - [User guide](docs/guides/user-guide.md) — commands, config, sessions, skills - [Architecture](docs/architecture/overview.md) — how the crates fit together and why - [Building an agent project](docs/agent/project-structure.md) — recommended structure - [Extension authoring](docs/extensions/authoring.md) — plugin templates and ABI rules - [Subagents](docs/extensions/subagents.md) — configuration inheritance, permissions and lifecycle - [Native RPC resource selection](docs/resource-selection-rpc.md) — exact startup Packages, Skills, extensions, instructions and tools (stage A) - [Local native resource management](docs/local-resource-management.md) — scoped snapshot install/inspect/update/remove, ownership, recovery and host leases (stage B) - [Remote mode](docs/remote/user-guide.md) — protocol, tokens, limitations - [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) - [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli) for per-crate API docs ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the build/test commands and the repository layout, and the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md) for what is already planned. Security problems should go through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), not a public issue. To submit a Rust extension from your own GitHub repository, open the [extension catalog](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/packages.html?lang=en) and select **Get listed**. The whole test suite runs offline: `cargo test --workspace --locked`. ## Acknowledgements Thank you to Mario Zechner and the [Pi contributors](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) for the original TypeScript SDK and the agent, tool and session designs that formed rpi's starting point. rpi reimplements that foundation in Rust and adds its own runtime and extension infrastructure; it does not load the TypeScript SDK or its npm extensions. Upstream copyright and MIT license notices are retained in [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). The `rpi-*` crates are a Rust-native coding-agent stack. ## Support If rpi helps you, consider buying the author a coffee. Donations support continued development and maintenance. Thank you!

# rpi · Rust 原生编码智能体运行时 [English](README.md) | **简体中文**

[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rpi-cli.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) [![下载量](https://img.shields.io/crates/d/rpi-cli.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rpi-cli) [![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/rpi-cli) [![许可证](https://img.shields.io/crates/l/rpi-cli.svg)](#许可证) [![MSRV](https://img.shields.io/badge/MSRV-1.88-blue.svg)](#安装) [![CI](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/bigfish1913/pi-rust?style=flat)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/stargazers) [![最新版本](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/bigfish1913/pi-rust)](https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/releases/latest) [![Best of Agent Harnesses](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%8F%86_Best_of-Agent_Harnesses-5ac4bf)](https://github.com/RyanAlberts/best-of-Agent-Harnesses) `rpi` 是用 Rust 编写、以库为核心的编码智能体运行时，并在其上提供了一个终端智能体。 工作区包含 11 个可组合的 crate，涵盖模型提供方适配、可从崩溃恢复的智能体循环、可复用的运行时、终端界面和稳定的插件 ABI。 你可以将同一套实现作为 SDK 嵌入应用，也可以直接运行 `rpi` 命令。 rpi 最初是 Mario Zechner 的 [Pi TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) 的 Rust 实现，现已具备自己的 Rust 原生插件 ABI 和执行基础设施。 上游项目的归属说明见[致谢](#致谢)和 [NOTICE](NOTICE)。 [快速上手](#快速上手) · [官网](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/) · [文档](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/docs.html) · [扩展目录与收录](https://rpi.bigfisharc.cn/packages.html?lang=zh) · [rpi-extension](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension) ## 演示 ![rpi 终端读取项目 README 并显示运行和测试命令](docs/images/rpi-interactive.png) **终端。** 在项目目录运行 `rpi`。图中展示隔离示例会话和一次 `read` 工具调用。[用户指南](docs/guides/user-guide.md) ![rpi-web 的项目侧栏、工具调用和 Markdown 回复](docs/images/rpi-web.png) **Web。** 运行 `rpi install rpi-web` 安装扩展，然后在项目目录运行 `rpi --webserver`，打开终端输出的地址。[Web 安装指南](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-extension/tree/main/packages/rpi-web) ![RPI Work 桌面预览，并排显示会话与 Git 差异](docs/images/rpi-work-desktop.png) **桌面端。** RPI Work 的 GPUI 预览版在原生窗口中展示项目会话、对话和 Git 差异。[RPI Work](https://github.com/pi-rust/rpi-work)
终端和 SDK 录屏 ![rpi 终端演示：无需请求模型即可打开内置帮助](docs/images/rpi-tui-demo.gif) 启动终端智能体后即可用 `/help` 查看帮助，无需真实 API 密钥或模型请求。录制脚本见 [`demo/tui.tape`](demo/tui.tape)。 ![rpi SDK 演示：通过 faux 提供方离线运行智能体循环和完整的工具调用](docs/images/rpi-sdk-demo.gif) 无需 API 密钥或网络，按测试所用的路径运行智能体循环和一次真实的 `write` 工具调用。录制脚本见 [`demo/sdk.tape`](demo/sdk.tape)，可用 `task demo` 重新生成。
## 三种用法 | 目标 | 所需依赖 | 从这里开始 | | --- | --- | --- | | 直接使用终端编码智能体 | 无需添加依赖 | `cargo install rpi-cli` | | 在自己的进程里运行智能体 | `rpi-agent`（可加 `rpi-ai`、`rpi-tools`） | [`examples/minimal`](examples/minimal) | | 为会话添加工具或模型提供方 | `rpi-plugin-sdk` | [`examples/plugin-stub`](examples/plugin-stub) | 三种用法共用一套实现。你可以在内嵌的智能体里调试工具，再把同一套代码打包成由全局 `rpi` 加载的 `cdylib` 插件。推荐的项目布局见[智能体项目结构](docs/agent/project-structure.md)。 ## 安装 **预编译二进制**（无需 Rust 工具链） ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/main/scripts/install.sh | sh ``` 脚本会验证发布的 SHA-256 校验值，再安装到 `/usr/local/bin` 或 `~/.local/bin`。可通过 `--dry-run` 预览安装操作。 在 **Windows (x64)** 上使用 PowerShell 5.1 或更高版本运行以下命令。 ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust/main/scripts/install.ps1).Content)) ``` 脚本会验证发布的 SHA-256 校验值，再安装到 `$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\rpi`。 按脚本输出的说明添加 PATH，然后运行 `rpi --version`。可附加 `-DryRun` 预览，或使用 `-Version ` 和 `-Dir 'C:\Tools\rpi'` 指定版本和目录。 **通过 npm 安装**（需要 Node.js 20 或更新版本，无需 Rust 工具链） ```bash npm install -g @bigfishnpm/rpi rpi --version ``` npm 安装器从 GitHub Releases 下载对应平台的二进制，并按包内固定的 SHA-256 校验值验证归档和可执行文件。 支持 macOS（x64/ARM64）、Windows（x64）和 Linux（x64 glibc/musl、ARM64 glibc）。 **通过 crates.io 安装**（需要 Rust 1.88 或更新版本） ```bash cargo install rpi-cli rpi --version ``` **通过包管理器安装** ```bash brew tap bigfish1913/tap && brew install rpi # macOS（Apple 芯片）、Linux scoop bucket add bigfish1913 https://github.com/bigfish1913/scoop-bucket scoop install rpi # Windows ``` 在 macOS 上，Homebrew 配方目前支持 Apple 芯片。Intel Mac 可以使用提供 `x86_64-apple-darwin` 产物的版本的预编译安装脚本，也可以运行 `cargo install rpi-cli`。[winget 安装清单正在审核](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/pull/444745)。 **从源码运行** ```bash git clone https://github.com/bigfish1913/pi-rust.git cd pi-rust && cargo run -p minimal # 离线智能体，无需 API 密钥 ``` 以下是两个离线示例的实际输出。两者都无需凭据或网络，每次运行的输出一致。用 `task demo-transcript` 可重新生成。 ```text $ cargo run -q -p minimal minimal example: 2 messages after run - user - assistant assistant reply: Hello from the faux provider! AgentEnd observed. $ cargo run -q -p tools-example tools example: 4 messages after run wrote out.txt (28 bytes): "hello from the tools example" AgentEnd observed; tool ran against OsExecutionEnv. ``` ## 快速上手 ### CLI ```bash export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... # 使用 OpenAI 时设置 OPENAI_API_KEY rpi # 交互式终端界面 rpi -p "总结这份 README" # 单次运行 rpi --mode json -p "列出所有 crate" # 机器可读的事件流 rpi --mini -p "解释这个错误" # 单次运行，结束后不保存会话 ``` `--mini` 使用内存会话并关闭原生持久化执行。进程退出时会话结束，该模式不支持会话导入、导出、分叉或恢复。上下文压缩、工具和资源发现仍可使用。用 `--tools read` 可将工具限制为 `read`，用 `-p` 可在单次回复后退出。 普通会话保存为 JSONL。运行中崩溃后，`rpi` 从最后一条已提交的帧恢复。 ### 模型配置 使用自定义 OpenAI 兼容网关时，将[示例 JSON](examples/models.example.json)另存为 `models.json`，放在下表所示的目录中。目录不存在时先创建。已有 `models.json` 时，把 `gateway` 条目加入现有的 `providers` 对象。 | 环境 | `models.json` 路径 | | --- | --- | | macOS / Linux | `~/.rpi/agent/models.json` | | Windows | `%USERPROFILE%\.rpi\agent\models.json` | | 自定义目录 | `RPI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` 指定的绝对目录下的 `models.json` | ```json { "providers": { "gateway": { "api": "openai-completions", "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1", "apiKey": "$RPI_GATEWAY_API_KEY", "models": [ { "id": "your-model-id", "name": "My Gateway Model" } ] } } } ``` 将 `baseUrl` 和 `your-model-id` 替换为提供方给出的地址和模型 ID，再在启动 rpi 的终端中设置密钥。 - macOS / Linux — `export RPI_GATEWAY_API_KEY='your-api-key'` - Windows PowerShell — `$env:RPI_GATEWAY_API_KEY = 'your-api-key'` ```bash rpi auth check --provider gateway rpi --model gateway/your-model-id ``` 启动命令中的模型 ID 要与 JSON 一致。[用户指南](docs/guides/user-guide.md#自定义-provider)也涵盖 Anthropic 兼容网关的配置。 ### 运行时诊断 要排查模型请求准备、上下文构建、工具执行或助手帧持久化的耗时，可临时把诊断输出到 stderr。 ```bash RPI_AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS=1 RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS=1 \ rpi -p "复现这个问题" 2>rpi-diagnostics.log ``` `RPI_AGENT_DIAGNOSTICS` 报告上下文、请求、工具和追加会话记录的耗时。`RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS` 报告持久化帧的批处理、刷新屏障及写入失败。 变量未设置或为 `0` 时诊断关闭。诊断输出与会话 JSONL 分开。 字段含义见 [Rust 调试指南](docs/debugging/rust-debugging.md)，也可以向内置只读 `docs` 工具传入 `{"topic":"debugging","query":"RPI_FRAME_DIAGNOSTICS"}` 查询。 ### 请求超时与模型兼容性 `--timeout 600` 限制整个 LLM 请求的耗时，包括流式响应。 响应开始后，`--stream-idle-timeout 300` 单独限制响应体连续未收到数据的时间。每个非空数据块都会重置空闲计时器，包括 SSE 心跳和不完整的帧。 流停滞会产生可重试的错误，是否重试取决于所配置的重试策略。持续接收数据的流可以运行超过空闲超时，直至达到总超时。 `--stream-idle-timeout 0` 可关闭空闲计时器。也可在 `~/.rpi/agent/settings.json` 中设置 `"streamIdleTimeout": 300`（单位为秒），命令行参数优先。 `httpIdleTimeout` 用于回收连接池内未使用的连接。 对于使用 `"api": "openai-completions"` 的提供方，在 `~/.rpi/agent/models.json` 中为每个模型设置 `compat` 对象，例如： ```json "compat": { "thinkingFormat": "deepseek", "requiresReasoningContent": true } ``` `requiresReasoningContent` 通过 `reasoning_content` 回传助手的推理内容，没有推理内容时使用空字符串。 也接受 Pi 的配置名 `requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages`。两个字段同时存在时，以 rpi 的字段为准，值冲突时会发出警告。 `thinkingFormat` 支持 `"openai"`（默认请求格式）和 `"deepseek"`（对具备推理能力的模型额外发送 `thinking: { "type": "enabled" | "disabled" }`）。 如果网关无法接收 `reasoning_effort`，可以用 `supportsReasoningEffort: false` 省略该字段。`requiresThinkingAsText` 会把推理内容放入普通文本。 未知字段和无效值会触发带有提供方及模型名的警告，无效的 `compat` 对象会被忽略。 ### SDK 使用进程内的确定性提供方构建智能体。示例无需 API 密钥或网络。 ```rust use rpi_agent::AgentBuilder; use rpi_ai::providers::faux::{FauxProvider, FauxScript}; use rpi_ai::Provider; #[tokio::main] async fn main() { // `FauxProvider::new` 已经返回 `Arc`。 let provider = FauxProvider::new(FauxScript::new().with_text("Hello from the faux provider!")); let model = provider.default_model().clone(); let agent = AgentBuilder::new() .model(model) .system_prompt("You are a helpful assistant.") .stream_fn(make_stream_fn(provider)) .build() .expect("agent builds"); let mut events = agent.subscribe(); agent.prompt("hi").await.expect("prompt completes"); while let Ok(ev) = events.try_recv() { let _ = ev; // AgentEvent::{MessageUpdate, ToolEnd, AgentEnd, …} } println!("{} messages after the run", agent.state().messages.len()); } ``` `make_stream_fn` 将同步 `StreamFn` 接口与异步提供方衔接。完整代码见 [`examples/minimal/src/main.rs`](examples/minimal/src/main.rs)，可通过 `cargo
